subject: research/verified-dse
professional: an EDA/physical-design researcher (MLCAD/DAC reviewer) who also knows multi-fidelity search statistics (Hyperband/BOHB, conformal prediction); first checks: are the rung scores and rank statistics computed correctly from the raw flow table, does the cached-table replay reproduce, and are negative results stated as such

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/rung_bias/analyse.py` on the committed results.jsonl: results.txt and summary.json regenerate with no git diff. Recomputed independently from raw jsonl fields with scipy.stats.kendalltau and numpy (not the repo's stats.py): mult8 tight R2 tau 0.503 (repo 0.50), pick regret 12.4% (repo 12.4); barrel16 relaxed tau 0.170, regret 15.1% (repo 0.17, 15.1); crc16 tight tau 0.719, regret 8.3% (repo 0.72, 8.3). Also brute-forced the O(n^2) rung inversion for 4 cells and it equals bound.inversion to 16 digits (e.g. alu8 tight 0.15199, barrel16 relaxed 0.27050). Also ran theory/bound.py, halving/replay.py, conformal/replay.py (0.4 s, 44 s, 38 s): git status clean, tables reproduce exactly. Not re-run: the Yosys/OpenROAD flow itself (neither tool is installed in this container), so raw flow numbers are taken as given; the 'routed' rung is global-route estimate plus repair_timing, which the README states.
evidence.completeness: Checked claimed items: README tables for milestones 1, 2, 9, 11 (M2 45 s row 0.94/0.61/1.08/1.27 matches experiments/search_baselines/results.txt); reproduce.sh lists ~60 analysis scripts and the three I ran ran clean; PAPER.md and paper/main.pdf exist, paper is stated as not submitted; 38 experiment directories each with results.txt. Open items are labelled as open (H5 unsupported, probabilistic bound open, no detail-route headline). No stub found. The programme has many milestones but only the cached-table replays are re-runnable here; flow rungs need OpenROAD.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 18 tests, OK (0.3 s). Seeded 4 mutations in core logic, reverting each with git checkout: (1) stats.kendall_tau_b concordance sign flipped -> 2 tests failed (caught); (2) bound.inversion tie-group min->max -> 5 failed (caught); (3) bound.pilot_top_inversion `s[b] <= s[a]` -> `<` (tie handling) -> all 18 passed (NOT caught); (4) stats.pick_regret `min(cheap)` -> `max(cheap)` (picks the worst rung point) -> all 18 passed (NOT caught). So the bound code is well tested (brute-force and random-instance checks) but the headline statistic of the whole programme, pick regret, has a test that does not constrain it. ~40 experiment directories have no tests beyond byte-identical regeneration of their own tables, which only detects drift, not a wrong formula.
evidence.craft: Read src/verified_dse/{stats,bound,flow}.py, experiments/rung_bias/analyse.py, reproduce.sh. Core library is small (258 lines), documented, stdlib-only, with a clear O(n log n) inversion and a brute-force cross-check. Defects: kth_inversion is O(n^2 log n) and tau is O(n^2) pure Python (fine at n=50); bootstrap_tau silently drops resamples where tau is undefined; flow.py regex-patches chip-pnr's pnr.tcl at run time and rewrites ' signed [' in netlists to suit OpenSTA 26Q3 (documented in a comment); experiments are one script per milestone with copied replay scaffolding rather than a shared harness; LOG.md is 283 KB.
evidence.claims: Checked: README M1/M2 numbers vs results.txt (match); 'R4 1.3 s cumulative' vs results.txt 'R4 total 0.80 (OpenROAD only)' (consistent, 0.8 + mapping); 10 ABC-rejected sequences (196 of 1200 failures, consistent with 20 per design); PAPER.md says 'not submitted' and states the negative headline. Does not back or is stale: README status line reads 'milestones 1 to 31 done (68: ...)' and lists milestones out of order with the numbering garbled, while the body documents milestones to 92; project.json lede/summary (the page text) still describes only 'milestones 1 to 3 done' and says H2 to H5 are 'not yet run', contradicting the README (H2 to H5 were run), so the live page under-reports and misdescribes the state. No unbacked positive result found; limits are stated per milestone, one corner/utilisation/tool-version is repeated in the Limitations.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it: pinned tool versions, cached tables (results.jsonl) so every replay runs without EDA tools in seconds to minutes, bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected tests at n=10, honest negative results. Nearest prior work (PROPOSAL.md, 12 ids checked with research/_shared/cite_check.py): multi-fidelity HPO (Hyperband, BOHB), conformal prediction, and open-flow ABC-script tuning; the new part is the measured rung bias on SKY130 for ABC pass sequences and the pilot-gated halving negative result. Novelty is modest (small designs, 50-point pools, global-route proxy) and mostly empirical; the regret bound (sum of cut rungs' inversions) is a three-line result that is sound but elementary. Publishable as a workshop-level negative-result paper (MLCAD), not yet as a strong venue paper.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard multi-fidelity practice (successive halving/Hyperband, BOHB replayed via TPE, GP-EI, conformal coverage) and physical-design practice (area x delay with WNS-adjusted period; tap cells excluded from final_area_notap; only global-route-estimated, which is acknowledged and a detail-route subsample is in experiments/detail_route). Departures: ten to thirty small combinational designs, one tt corner (second ss corner added), 50 pool points so strategies saturate; a PD engineer would say the routed reference is not signoff and designs are far from industrial size; a statistician would want the n=10 design-level tests, which the repo itself reports as not surviving Holm.

defects.what: Seeded mutation: pick_regret(min -> max), i.e. choosing the worst point on the cheap rung, passes all 18 tests; the programme's headline metric is effectively untested
Seeded mutation: pilot_top_inversion tie handling (<= to <) passes all 18 tests
Page text (project.json lede and summary) says milestones 1 to 3 done and H2 to H5 not yet run; README documents H2 to H5 run through milestone 92. The live page is stale and contradicts the README
README status line garbled: 'milestones 1 to 31 done (68: ...)' with milestones listed out of order; a reader cannot tell the current milestone
Flow rungs (the raw data source) could not be re-run here; no EDA tools in the container, so raw routed numbers rest on the committed table
bootstrap_tau silently drops resamples with undefined tau, and reproducibility gate (git diff) detects drift but not a wrong formula

verdict: A real, careful, honestly negative multi-fidelity study. Every statistic I recomputed from raw rows with scipy/numpy and a brute-force inversion matched the repo exactly, and the cached-table analyses I re-ran regenerate byte-identically. It is finished against what it claims (completeness 3) and a researcher could build on it. It does not meet the bar because verification is 2: two of four seeded core-logic mutations, including the one that flips pick regret to choose the worst point, pass the 18 tests, and the experiments are guarded only by regeneration. Claims is 2 because the page text in project.json is stale at 'milestones 1 to 3' and contradicts the README, and the README status line is garbled. The science is a modest, sound, workshop-level negative result on small designs with a global-route proxy.
